examples.ko: 이번 우승의 가장 큰 공로자는 골키퍼예요.
examples.en: The biggest contributor to this victory is the goalkeeper.

examples.ko: 마을 발전에 힘쓴 공로자들에게 상을 드렸어요.
examples.en: We gave awards to the people who contributed to the village's development.
She is the unsung hero of this project.
I was chosen as a distinguished contributor and received a certificate of commendation.

examples.ko: 공로자를 위한 작은 행사가 내일 열려요.
examples.en: A small event for the contributors will be held tomorrow.
People are curious who the real contributor is.

explain: '일등 공로자', '숨은 공로자'처럼 칭찬할 때 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '일등 공신'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used in praise, as in '일등 공로자' (top contributor) and '숨은 공로자' (unsung hero). A similar expression is '일등 공신'.

examples.ko: 사람들은 이것을 금세기 최고의 발명품이라고 불러요.
examples.en: People call this the best invention of this century.

examples.ko: 이 작가는 금세기 가장 위대한 소설가로 평가받아요.
examples.en: This author is regarded as the greatest novelist of this century.

examples.ko: 금세기에 들어와 기술이 정말 빨리 발전했어요.
examples.en: Since entering this century, technology has developed really fast.

examples.ko: 금세기 중반에는 인구가 줄어들 것이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the population will shrink by the middle of this century.
We are people living in this century.

examples.ko: 금세기 들어 날씨가 이상해졌다고 말하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the weather has become strange in this century.

explain: '이번 세기'보다 격식 있는 글말이에요. 쓰는 때에 따라 가리키는 세기가 달라지는데, 요즘은 보통 21세기를 말해요. '금세기 최고의 발명'처럼 평가하는 글에서 많이 봐요. 발음이 비슷한 '금세'(곧)와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a more formal, written way to say 'this century'. Which century it points to depends on when it is written, and today it usually means the 21st. You often see it in evaluations like '금세기 최고의 발명'. It is completely different from the similar-sounding '금세' (soon).

examples.ko: 그 가수의 무대 의상은 꽤 도발적이에요.
examples.en: That singer's stage outfit is quite provocative.
He answered the provocative question calmly.
Many people say the ad is too provocative.
His way of speaking sounded provocative, and it upset me.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 색이 강하고 도발적이어서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: This painting has strong colors and is provocative, so it stands out.

examples.ko: 그의 태도는 도발적이지 않고 아주 부드러웠어요.
examples.en: His attitude was not provocative at all and was very gentle.

explain: '도발적이다', '도발적인 ~'처럼 써요. 말이나 행동에서는 상대를 자극해서 싸움을 거는 느낌이고, 패션이나 광고에서는 과감하고 시선을 끄는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used as '도발적이다' or '도발적인 ~'. For words and actions it feels like provoking someone into a fight, while for fashion or ads it feels bold and attention-grabbing.

examples.en: On the weekend I rode a bike on the Han River bank.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 둔치 주차장이 물에 잠겨요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, the riverside parking lot gets flooded.
We spread a mat on the riverside and ate fried chicken.
Every evening I run along the riverside.

examples.ko: 강 둔치에는 운동 시설이 잘 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The riverside has good exercise facilities.
Access to the riverside was blocked because of the flood.

explain: '강가'와 비슷하지만, 물가 옆에 평평하게 만들어 놓은 공원이나 운동 공간을 가리킬 때가 많아요. '한강 둔치'처럼 강 이름과 같이 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '강가' (riverside), but it often points to the flat park or exercise area made beside the water. It is often used with a river name, as in '한강 둔치'.

examples.en: People stood in a ring around the scene of the accident.

examples.ko: 아이들이 선생님 주위에 둘러서서 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: The kids stood around the teacher and listened to the story.
Everyone, please gather in a circle around the cake.

examples.ko: 구경꾼들이 길거리 공연 앞에 둘러서 있어요.
examples.en: Onlookers are standing in a circle in front of the street performance.
The people standing around clapped.

examples.ko: 그냥 둘러서 있지만 말고 좀 도와주세요.
examples.en: Don't just stand around, please help a little.

explain: 가운데에 있는 사람이나 물건을 향해 동그랗게 서는 모습을 말해요. 앉아서 그렇게 할 때는 '둘러앉다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes standing in a circle facing a person or thing in the middle. When people do the same while sitting, it is '둘러앉다'.

examples.en: I went to the restroom for a moment during the play's intermission.

examples.ko: 공연 막간을 이용해 음료를 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I used the break between acts to buy a drink.
We did a small quiz as an interlude event.

examples.ko: 막간의 휴식 시간이 십 분이라서 서둘렀어요.
examples.en: The intermission was only ten minutes, so I hurried.

examples.ko: 촬영 막간에도 배우들은 대본을 읽고 있었어요.
examples.en: Even between takes, the actors were reading their scripts.
The interlude video was fun, so it wasn't boring.

explain: 원래 연극에서 막과 막 사이를 뜻해서 공연, 촬영, 행사 이야기에서 잘 나와요. 일반적인 짧은 쉬는 시간은 '짬'이나 '쉬는 시간'이라고 해야 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It originally means the time between acts in a play, so it appears mostly in talk about performances, filming and events. For an ordinary short break, '짬' or '쉬는 시간' sounds more natural.

examples.en: If you want to sit in on a trial, you have to apply in advance.

examples.ko: 친구와 같이 방송 녹화를 방청하러 갔어요.
examples.en: I went with a friend to be in the audience for a TV recording.

examples.ko: 국회 회의를 방청해 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have attended a National Assembly meeting as a spectator before.
Please turn off your phone while you are in the audience.
My family attended the public debate as spectators.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 누구나 무료로 방청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can watch this program in person for free.

explain: 재판, 국회, 방송 녹화처럼 공개된 자리에서 지켜볼 때 써요. 영화나 공연은 그냥 '보다'를 쓰고 방청하다는 쓰지 않아요. 가는 사람은 '방청객'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for watching in person at open events such as trials, National Assembly sessions and TV recordings. For movies or performances you just say '보다', not 방청하다. The people who attend are called '방청객'.

examples.en: The actor is putting on makeup in the dressing room.
I sent flowers to the dressing room before the show.
The dressing room is behind the stage.
I knocked on the dressing room door and went in.
The singer is practicing a song inside the dressing room.

examples.ko: 분장실이 좁아서 여러 명이 함께 써요.
examples.en: The dressing room is small, so several people share it.

explain: 연극, 방송, 공연에서 배우나 가수가 분장하고 옷을 갈아입는 곳이에요. 가게의 '탈의실'이나 '피팅룸'과는 달라요. 방송국에서는 '대기실'이라는 말도 같이 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the place where actors and singers do their makeup and change in theater, TV and concerts. It is different from a shop's '탈의실' or '피팅룸'. At TV stations people also often say '대기실' (waiting room).

examples.ko: 그 선수는 팀 개혁의 선봉장 역할을 했어요.
examples.en: That player acted as the spearhead of the team's reform.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 친환경 사업의 선봉장이 되고 싶대요.
examples.en: I hear this company wants to be the leader of eco-friendly business.
My older brother stepped forward as the leader of the opposition movement.
Students were at the forefront of the environmental campaign.

examples.ko: 동생이 대청소의 선봉장이라며 제일 먼저 나섰어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling said they were leading the big cleanup and stepped up first.

examples.ko: 선봉장에 선 사람은 책임도 크다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think the person at the head of the charge also carries great responsibility.

explain: '~의 선봉장'처럼 어떤 일을 맨 앞에서 이끄는 사람이나 팀을 비유해서 말할 때 많이 써요. '리더'보다 앞장서서 뛰어드는 느낌이 강하고, 실제 군대 이야기보다 개혁·운동·경기 이야기에 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly used figuratively, as in '~의 선봉장', for the person or team that leads from the very front. It feels more like charging ahead than a plain 'leader', and it appears more in talk of reforms, movements and sports than of real armies.

examples.ko: 어제 열린 시장 행사가 성황을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: The market event held yesterday was a great success.
I'm so happy the concert ended with a packed, successful crowd.
The shop's opening ceremony was a big, crowded success.

examples.ko: 공연이 매일 성황이라서 표 구하기가 어려워요.
examples.en: The show is packed every day, so tickets are hard to get.

examples.ko: 동네 축제가 성황 속에 막을 내렸어요.
examples.en: The neighborhood festival came to an end amid a lively turnout.
It's a small shop, but it's always busy with customers.

explain: 행사, 공연, 가게처럼 사람이 많이 모여서 잘되는 모습을 말해요. '성황을 이루다'와 '성황리에 끝나다'가 가장 많이 쓰이고, 사람이 없을 때는 반대로 '썰렁하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes events, shows and shops that draw a big crowd and go well. The most common forms are '성황을 이루다' and '성황리에 끝나다'. When nobody shows up, people say '썰렁하다' instead.

examples.en: We make the stage props for the play ourselves.

examples.ko: 소도구 담당을 맡은 친구가 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: The friend in charge of props looks busy.

examples.ko: 무대에 필요한 소도구를 미리 준비해 두세요.
examples.en: Please prepare the props needed for the stage in advance.

examples.ko: 이 사진관에는 촬영용 소도구가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: This photo studio has a lot of props for shoots.

examples.ko: 작은 소도구도 연기에 큰 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Even a small prop is a big help to acting.
We decided to use a hat and a cane as props.

explain: 연극, 영화, 사진 촬영에서 배우가 들거나 쓰는 작은 물건을 말해요. 무대 배경처럼 큰 것은 '대도구'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '소품'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to small items actors hold or use in plays, films and photo shoots. Large things such as stage backdrops are called '대도구'. A similar word is '소품'.

en: from start to finish; all the time; all the way

examples.ko: 그는 면접 내내 시종 웃는 얼굴이었어요.
examples.en: He had a smile on his face throughout the whole interview.
The presentation went on in a calm atmosphere from start to finish.
Our team was ahead the whole game.

examples.ko: 그녀는 시종 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: She didn't say a word the entire time.

examples.ko: 그는 시종일관 같은 태도로 손님을 대했어요.
examples.en: He treated customers with the same attitude consistently throughout.

examples.ko: 시종 불안해하던 친구도 결과를 듣고 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend, who had been anxious the whole time, smiled when hearing the result.

explain: 처음부터 끝까지 한결같다는 뜻으로, '시종일관'이라는 덩어리로 가장 많이 써요. 말보다는 글, 뉴스, 발표에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '내내', '계속'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It conveys that something stayed the same from beginning to end, and is most often used in the chunk '시종일관'. It appears more in writing, news and presentations, while '내내' or '계속' is more natural in everyday talk.

examples.en: I'm studying botany at university.
The botany professor holds class in the forest.
A botanist named the new flower.

examples.ko: 이 책은 식물학에 관심 있는 사람에게 좋아요.
examples.en: This book is good for people interested in botany.
My younger sibling wants to get into the botany department.

examples.ko: 식물학 연구는 환경 보호에도 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Botanical research also helps protect the environment.

explain: 식물을 연구하는 학문이고, 동물을 연구하는 '동물학'과 짝을 이뤄요. 연구하는 사람은 '식물학자'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the field that studies plants, and it pairs with '동물학', the study of animals. A person who does this research is a '식물학자'.

examples.en: The soldiers marched majestically.
The pine tree standing on the mountaintop looks imposing.
The lion walked toward us with a commanding presence.
Even the once-majestic castle has now collapsed.
My father in a suit looks especially dignified today.
That general looked truly majestic.

explain: 사람, 동물, 건물이 크고 힘 있어 보여서 감탄할 만할 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. '위풍당당하게 걷다/행진하다/서 있다'처럼 모습이나 걸음과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for a person, animal or building that looks big and powerful enough to impress you. It often goes with appearance or movement, as in '위풍당당하게 걷다/행진하다/서 있다'.

examples.en: All of the staff sincerely thank our customers.

examples.ko: 가족 일동은 할머니 생신을 함께 축하드렸어요.
examples.en: The whole family congratulated Grandma together on her birthday.
We sent a notice text to all the students.
At the end of the letter, it said 'All employees'.
We prepared a gift in the name of all the friends.

examples.ko: 선생님께 반 학생 일동이 쓴 편지를 드렸어요.
examples.en: I gave the teacher a letter written by all the students in the class.

explain: '직원 일동', '가족 일동'처럼 사람 모임 뒤에 붙여서 그 모임 모두를 한꺼번에 가리켜요. 공지문, 편지, 인사말에서 자주 보고, 말할 때는 '다 같이'나 '모두'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is attached after a group of people, as in '직원 일동' or '가족 일동', to mean everyone in that group together. You often see it in notices, letters and greetings, and in speech people also say '다 같이' or '모두'.

en: pile of earth; heap of soil

examples.en: A heap of earth from the landslide blocked the road.

examples.ko: 공사장 한쪽에 흙더미를 높이 쌓아 두었어요.
examples.en: They piled the soil high on one side of the construction site.
A car was buried under the heap of earth in the landslide.
The kids are playing happily on top of the pile of dirt.
They are moving the pile of soil with an excavator.
A rain-soaked pile of earth collapses easily.

explain: 흙이 쌓여 있는 전체 모양을 말해서 공사장이나 사고 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 흙이 한 덩어리로 뭉친 것은 '흙덩이'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: It describes soil piled up as a whole, so it often appears in construction sites and accident news. A single lump of earth is called '흙덩이', which is different.
